subject: stack
message: The map shows no space set aside for the stack. The tool looked for an output section with "stack" in its name and a size above zero, or a step of the location counter by _Min_Stack_Size, __stack_size__, __STACK_SIZE, __stack_size and 5 more inside a section, and found none. It found _estack = 0x20005000 (line 70), which says where the stack is, not how much room it gets. The linker checks only what is placed in a region, so the stack is not in the totals above and can grow into the data below it with no error at link time.
basis: A section with no contents may be allocatable, which means that an area in memory should be set aside, but nothing in particular should be loaded there (in some cases this memory must be zeroed out). If the combined output sections directed to a memory region are too large for the region, the linker will issue an error message.
fix: Reserve the stack in the linker script: a section in RAM that steps the location counter by the stack size (for example ". = . + _Min_Stack_Size;"), so the linker counts it and stops the link when RAM is too small.

subject: heap
message: The firmware takes memory at run time: the map holds _sbrk (line 160) and _malloc_r (line 171). It shows no space set aside for the heap: the tool looked for an output section with "heap" in its name and a size above zero, or a step of the location counter by _Min_Heap_Size, __heap_size__, __HEAP_SIZE, __heap_size and 5 more inside a section, and found none. The heap is then not in the totals above, and malloc can run into the stack with no error at link time.
basis: A section with no contents may be allocatable, which means that an area in memory should be set aside, but nothing in particular should be loaded there (in some cases this memory must be zeroed out). If the combined output sections directed to a memory region are too large for the region, the linker will issue an error message.
fix: Reserve the heap in the linker script, as for the stack (for example ". = . + _Min_Heap_Size;" in a section in RAM), and let _sbrk stop at the end of that space. If the firmware should not allocate at run time, remove the calls to malloc.

subject: .ccmram
message: The output section ".ccmram" (2,560 bytes at 0x10000000) lies outside every region of the Memory Configuration table (FLASH and RAM), so the linker did not count it against a region, and this report cannot either.
basis: Once you define a memory region, you can direct the linker to place specific output sections into that memory region by using the '>region' output section attribute. Orphan sections are sections present in the input files which are not explicitly placed into the output file by the linker script.
fix: Declare the memory it is meant for with the MEMORY command and place the section there with ">REGION", or move its input sections into a section that is placed in a region.

subject: .data
message: The output section ".data" (404 bytes) runs in "RAM" at 0x20000000 and is loaded from "FLASH" at 0x080100b8. Its initial values are stored in "FLASH" and copied to "RAM" by the startup code, so the same 404 bytes count in both regions.
basis: An example of when they might be different is when a data section is loaded into ROM, and then copied into RAM when the program starts up (this technique is often used to initialize global variables in a ROM based system). In this case the ROM address would be the LMA, and the RAM address would be the VMA.
fix: Nothing to fix; this is how initialised data works. To save space in both regions, make data that never changes const (it then stays in "FLASH" only) and leave data that starts at zero uninitialised (it then goes to .bss, which takes no space in "FLASH").
